- `facilityId?: string`

It also reads the `continue_draft` query param via `useQueryParams()` (QuestionnaireForm.tsx:378) to resume drafts.

## 2. State management

All local `useState`, no form library (QuestionnaireForm.tsx:380-389):
- `questionnaireForms: QuestionnaireFormState[]` — THE core state. `QuestionnaireFormState = { questionnaire: QuestionnaireRead; responses: QuestionnaireResponse[]; errors: QuestionValidationError[] }` (QuestionnaireForm.tsx:63-67). One entry per questionnaire in the session (multi-questionnaire).
- `serverErrors: ServerValidationError[]` — `{reference_id, message, status_code}` (QuestionnaireForm.tsx:76-80)
- `isDirty` — drives `useNavigationPrompt` unsaved-changes guard (skipped in DEV) (QuestionnaireForm.tsx:586)
- `activeQuestionnaireId` / `activeGroupId` — left-nav scroll highlighting (QuestionnaireForm.tsx:948-965)
- `isInitialized`, `draftMismatchError`

Fetching:
- Questionnaire definition: `GET /api/v1/questionnaire/{id}/` via `questionnaireApi.get` (QuestionnaireForm.tsx:391-401; route at src/types/questionnaire/questionnaireApi.ts:20-24) — **skipped** when the id is in `FIXED_QUESTIONNAIRES` (client-side synthetic questionnaires, see §6).
- Draft: `GET /api/v1/form_submission/{external_id}/` when `continue_draft` present (QuestionnaireForm.tsx:404-416; src/types/questionnaire/formSubmissionApi.ts:21-25).

Initialization effect (QuestionnaireForm.tsx:588-639): resolves `FIXED_QUESTIONNAIRES[questionnaireId] || questionnaireData`, then seeds `questionnaireForms` with `initializeResponses()`. Draft path restores `draftData.response_dump.questionnaireResponses` (the whole `QuestionnaireFormState` was dumped), with an id-mismatch guard (QuestionnaireForm.tsx:602-606).

`initializeResponses` (QuestionnaireForm.tsx:334-367): flattens groups recursively; creates one `QuestionnaireResponse` per leaf question `{question_id, link_id, values: [], structured_type: q.structured_type ?? null}`. Pre-fills `values` from `answer_option[].initial_selected` as `{type:"string", value, coding: opt.code}` entries.

## 3. How responses accumulate

- Rendering: each form renders `<QuestionRenderer questions responses onResponseChange .../>` (QuestionnaireForm.tsx:1051-1100) → `QuestionGroup` per top-level question (src/components/Questionnaire/QuestionRenderer.tsx:66-96) → `QuestionInput` per leaf.
- `onResponseChange(values: ResponseValue[], questionId, note?)` **replaces the whole `values` array** for the matching `question_id` and clears that form's `errors: []` wholesale (QuestionnaireForm.tsx:1058-1081). Repeating questions are just multiple entries in `values` (QuestionInput manages the array, src/components/Questionnaire/QuestionTypes/QuestionInput.tsx:197-213).
- `clearError(questionId)` removes one error entry (QuestionnaireForm.tsx:1086-1099).
- Conditionality: `isQuestionEnabled(question, responses)` in src/components/Questionnaire/QuestionTypes/QuestionGroup.tsx:37-102 — matches `enable_when[].question` against `link_id`, normalizes booleans to `"Yes"/"No"` strings (QuestionGroup.tsx:51-55), supports exists/equals/not_equals/greater/less/gte/lte, `enable_behavior: "any" | "all"`.
- Scribe plugin hook: `<PLUGIN_Component __name="Scribe" formState setFormState/>` gets full read/write access to `questionnaireForms` (QuestionnaireForm.tsx:1189-1193; src/pluginTypes.ts:18-27).

## 4. Validation (client side, in `handleSubmit`)

QuestionnaireForm.tsx:743-827:
1. Clear all errors.
2. Recursive `validateQuestion` per form:
   - Required check (only if `isQuestionEnabled`): a question passes if any `values` entry has non-empty `value` (arrays must be non-empty) OR has `coding` OR `unit` (QuestionnaireForm.tsx:761-787). Failure pushes `{question_id, error: t("field_required"), type: "validation_error"}`.
   - Structured check: `STRUCTURED_TYPE_VALIDATORS` map (QuestionnaireForm.tsx:295-332) — **only 5 of 11 structured types have validators**: `appointment`, `encounter`, `medication_statement`, `medication_request`, `files` (delegating to `validate*Question` exports in the respective QuestionTypes components). allergy/diagnosis/symptom/service_request/charge_item/time_of_death have no client validation.
3. `setQuestionnaireForms(formsWithValidation)`; if any error, scroll to `document.getElementById("question-" + firstErrorId)` and abort (QuestionnaireForm.tsx:819-827).

Error display: `ValidationErrorDisplay` (QuestionnaireForm.tsx:96-293) renders both form-level errors and server errors with "scroll to question" buttons (uses `question-{id}` DOM ids and `structured_type` back-mapping at QuestionnaireForm.tsx:142-155). Submit button also disabled while `hasErrors` (QuestionnaireForm.tsx:715, 1165).

## 5. Submission — the important part

**Everything goes through ONE batch call**: `POST /api/v1/batch_requests/` (`batchApi.batchRequest`, src/types/base/batch/batchApi.ts:11-18; body shape `{requests: [{url, method, reference_id, body}]}`, src/types/base/batch/batch.ts:11-18). The mutation is `mutate(batchApi.batchRequest, { silent: true })` (QuestionnaireForm.tsx:418-422) — silent suppresses the global error toast; component handles errors itself.

Request assembly order in `handleSubmit` (QuestionnaireForm.tsx:829-946):

**(a) Structured questions FIRST** (QuestionnaireForm.tsx:830-857). For every response with `structured_type` and a non-empty array in `values[0].value`, call `getStructuredRequests(type, data, {facilityId, patientId, encounterId})` (async; awaited via `Promise.all`). Handlers in src/components/Questionnaire/structured/handlers.ts:34-268 build **raw domain-API requests**, one per structured type — structured answers NEVER go to the questionnaire submit endpoint:
- `allergy_intolerance` → `POST /api/v1/patient/{patientId}/allergy_intolerance/upsert/` `{datapoints: [...]}` (handlers.ts:45) — skipped without encounterId
- `medication_request` → `POST /api/v1/patient/{patientId}/medication/request/upsert/` — only `dirty` rows; new rows get `create_prescription` with generated `alternate_identifier` (handlers.ts:62-92)
- `medication_statement` → `POST .../medication/statement/upsert/` (handlers.ts:103)
- `symptom` → `POST .../symptom/upsert/` (handlers.ts:125)
- `diagnosis` → `POST .../diagnosis/upsert/` — only `dirty` rows (handlers.ts:141-160)
- `encounter` → `PUT /api/v1/encounter/{encounterId}/` (update, not create; requires facilityId) (handlers.ts:163-188)
- `appointment` → `POST /api/v1/facility/{facilityId}/slots/{slot_id}/create_appointment/` (handlers.ts:189-205)
- `files` → one `POST /api/v1/files/upload-file/` per file, `file_data` converted to base64 via `readFileAsDataURL` (handlers.ts:206-225)
- `time_of_death` → `PUT /api/v1/patient/{patientId}/` `{deceased_datetime}` (handlers.ts:226-237)
- `charge_item` → `POST /api/v1/facility/{facilityId}/charge_item/apply_charge_item_defs/` (handlers.ts:238-251)
- `service_request` → `POST /api/v1/facility/{facilityId}/service_request/apply_activity_definition/` (handlers.ts:252-267)
Each carries `reference_id = structured type name` (used to map server errors back).

**(b) Regular answers per questionnaire** (QuestionnaireForm.tsx:859-924). Filter: not structured, `values.length > 0`, `values[0].value !== ""`, and question currently enabled (re-checked via `findQuestionById` + `isQuestionEnabled`, QuestionnaireForm.tsx:877-885). Then push:
```
url: `/api/v1/questionnaire/${form.questionnaire.id}/submit/`   // ID, not slug
method: "POST"
reference_id: form.questionnaire.id
body: {
  resource_id: encounterId ?? patientId,   // line 873
  encounter: encounterId,
  patient: patientId,
  results: [{ question_id, values: [...], note, body_site, method }]
}
```
Value serialization (QuestionnaireForm.tsx:888-916): `date` → `dateQueryString` (yyyy-MM-dd, invalid dates become `""`); `dateTime` → `toISOString()`; entries with `unit` → `{value: value?.toString(), unit, coding}`; coding-only → `{coding}`; everything else → `{value: String(value)}`.
Note: `questionnaireApi.submit` (src/types/questionnaire/questionnaireApi.ts:49-65) declares a *different, stale* body (`responses[].value` singular) — the form bypasses that typed route entirely and hand-builds the URL.

**(c) Draft finalization** (QuestionnaireForm.tsx:927-942): if resuming a draft, append `PUT /api/v1/form_submission/{continueDraftId}/` with `status: "submitted"` and full `response_dump`, `reference_id: form_submission_{id}`.

Then `setIsDirty(false); submitBatch({ requests })` (QuestionnaireForm.tsx:944-945).

**Success**: clear server errors, toast, call `onSubmit?.()` (QuestionnaireForm.tsx:423-427).

**Error handling per request** (QuestionnaireForm.tsx:428-511): batch endpoint returns non-2xx when any sub-request fails; `HTTPError.cause` carries the body (src/Utils/request/query.ts:53-65). `error.cause.results` is filtered to `status_code !== 200`; each failed result becomes a `ServerValidationError` — message built from pydantic-style `{errors: [{loc, msg}]}` (both array-of-objects and object forms handled, QuestionnaireForm.tsx:466-489). Results whose `data.errors[]` contain `question_id` are additionally routed to `handleSubmissionError` (QuestionnaireForm.tsx:676-713) which attaches per-question errors to forms — **note it maps `results[index] → questionnaireForms[index]` by array position, which is only correct by accident** (failed-results index ≠ form index when structured/multiple requests are present). Ends with a generic failure toast.

## 6. Fixed/structured pseudo-questionnaires

`FIXED_QUESTIONNAIRES` in src/components/Questionnaire/data/StructuredFormData.tsx:262-271 — 11 client-side synthetic `QuestionnaireRead` objects keyed by slug (`encounter`, `medication_request`, `allergy_intolerance`, `medication_statement`, `service_request`, `diagnosis`, `symptom`, `files`, `time_of_death`, `charge_item`, `appointment`), each containing a single required `type:"structured"` question. `StructuredQuestionType` derives from this list (StructuredFormData.tsx:273-274). This is how e.g. route `/facility/:fid/patient/:pid/consultation` renders "create encounter" as a questionnaire (`questionnaireId="encounter"`).

## 7. Drafts (save-as-draft)

- Gated by `careConfig.enableQuestionnaireDraft` (care.config.ts:333) AND exactly one questionnaire in session AND zero structured questions (`isDraftSaveable`, QuestionnaireForm.tsx:556-582).
- Create: `POST /api/v1/form_submission/` `{patient, questionnaire: slug, encounter, status: "draft", response_dump: {questionnaireResponses: <QuestionnaireFormState>}}` (QuestionnaireForm.tsx:717-741; types src/types/questionnaire/formSubmission.ts:9-18). Update: `PUT /api/v1/form_submission/{id}/`. Both navigate to the encounter updates page on success (QuestionnaireForm.tsx:514-549).

## 8. QuestionnaireSearch & multi-questionnaire sessions

`QuestionnaireSearch` — src/components/Questionnaire/QuestionnaireSearch.tsx:48-191:
- Popover (desktop) / Drawer (mobile) + cmdk Command list; opens lazily (`enabled: isOpen`).
- Fetches `GET /api/v1/questionnaire/` via `query.debounced(questionnaireApi.list, {queryParams: {title: search, subject_type (conditional), status: "active"}})` (QuestionnaireSearch.tsx:61-73).
- Default `onSelect` navigates relative to `questionnaire/{id}` (QuestionnaireSearch.tsx:52); callers usually override.

# Where clinicians FILL questionnaires and view CLINICAL HISTORY in care_fe

## 1. Fill-flow routes (the mounting surface)

All fill routes live in `src/Routers/routes/ConsultationRoutes.tsx` and mount **`EncounterQuestionnaire`** (`src/components/Patient/EncounterQuestionnaire.tsx`):

| Route | Mounts | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `/facility/:facilityId/patient/:patientId/encounter/:encounterId/questionnaire` | `EncounterQuestionnaire subjectType="encounter"` (ConsultationRoutes.tsx:96-104) | blank picker — user searches a form |
| `.../encounter/:encounterId/questionnaire/:questionnaireId` | same + `questionnaireId` (ConsultationRoutes.tsx:106-115) | `:questionnaireId` may be a UUID **or** a fixed-slug pseudo-form |
| `/facility/:facilityId/patient/:patientId/consultation` | `questionnaireId="encounter"` (ConsultationRoutes.tsx:134-144) | encounter-creation via structured "encounter" question |
| `/facility/:facilityId/patient/:patientId/questionnaire` and `/patient/:patientId/questionnaire` | `subjectType="patient"` (ConsultationRoutes.tsx:145-157) | patient-subject "updates" fill |

Sidebar is suppressed for the encounter fill route only, via regex in `src/Routers/AppRouter.tsx:53-54` (`PATHS_WITHOUT_SIDEBAR`); the questionnaire studio fullscreen routes are at AppRouter.tsx:55-57. Patient-subject fill routes still render the sidebar.

**`EncounterQuestionnaire`** (EncounterQuestionnaire.tsx:25-87) is a thin shell: fetches encounter (`encounterApi.get`), renders `PatientHeader` + `PatientDeceasedInfo` above a `Card` wrapping `QuestionnaireForm`, and on submit navigates to `.../encounter/{encounterId}/updates`, `/facility/{f}/patient/{p}/updates`, or `/patient/{p}/updates` (lines 68-80). **This is the component a rebuilt fill experience replaces/re-implements; the routes above are the contract.**

## 2. The legacy fill engine

# Questionnaire Fill Experience (v2) — Design Spec

Date: 2026-08-02
Status: DRAFT — autonomous run (user directive; interactive gates skipped).
Reference UI: Figma `Care - Master` node `43604-21509` (section: 8 "Patient
Encounter questionnaire" frames + 2 "Encounter_Overview_in-progress" frames).
Branch: `bodhi/questionnaire-fill` (new), stacked PR onto
`bodhi/questionnaire-wysiwyg-builder` (#16619 → #16618 → develop).

## Goal

Re-engineer the clinician data-entry ("fill") experience on the v2 engine:

- The Figma reference: a two-tab fill page — tab 1 is the questionnaire
  data-entry canvas, tab 2 is a clinical-history section — replacing the
  legacy `EncounterQuestionnaire` + `QuestionnaireForm` page.
- Local autosave: simple interruptions (reload, crash, accidental nav) must
  not lose in-progress answers.
- Structured questions re-architected behind one extensible contract so new
  structured types are added in one place, not five.
- Stacked PR, new branch; rearchitect whatever the quality bar needs.

User directives, verbatim intent: "the user needs to be re-engineered now";
"reference implementation as 2 tabs, 2nd tab is clinical history section";
"data entry section should also support autosave in local so that simple
interruptions doesn't clear the data"; "The structured should be engineered
correctly so that we can also add more structured questions later"; "work a
new branch and make it a stack PR"; "feel free to rearchitect everything
required to make this a maintainable high quality system".

## Current state (evidence)

- v2 `form/` renderer is fill-ready except the host: `FormMode` already has
  `"fill"`; `validation.ts:collectRequiredErrors` is a pure seam with no
  caller; `errorsAtom` has readers and no writer; `StructuredSlot` passes a
  stub `clearError`; every block carries a `data-question-id` scroll anchor
  (see `QuestionnaireV2/README.md` + form-engine map).
- Legacy fill (`src/components/Questionnaire/QuestionnaireForm.tsx`, ~1200
  lines) is the behavior reference: one `batchApi.batchRequest` call —
  structured answers become raw domain-API requests via

# Structured Question Types — Full Map (care_fe)

## 1. Type system / source of truth

- `"structured"` is one of 14 `QUESTION_TYPES` — `src/types/questionnaire/question.ts:8-25`; a Question carries `structured_type?: StructuredQuestionType` at `question.ts:150`.
- **`StructuredQuestionType` is derived from a component-layer data file**, not from `src/types`: `src/components/Questionnaire/data/StructuredFormData.tsx:273-274` (`(typeof STRUCTURED_QUESTIONS)[number]["value"]`). The 11 values (`StructuredFormData.tsx:212-260`): `allergy_intolerance`, `medication_request`, `medication_statement`, `symptom`, `diagnosis`, `encounter`, `time_of_death`, `files`, `service_request`, `charge_item`, `appointment`.
- Each entry also carries a hardcoded single-question "fixed questionnaire" (e.g. `encounterQuestionnaire` at `StructuredFormData.tsx:3-20`), collected into `FIXED_QUESTIONNAIRES` (`:262-271`) — these short-circuit the API fetch in `QuestionnaireForm.tsx:400,591` so `/questionnaire/allergy_intolerance` etc. work without a backend record. `filterStructuredQuestionnaireSlugs` (`:276-283`) strips those synthetic slugs before template-list queries (`MedicationRequestQuestion.tsx:467`, `ServiceRequestQuestion.tsx:448`).
- **Inverted dependency**: `src/types/questionnaire/question.ts:1`, `form.ts:1`, and `structured/types.ts:1` all import the type FROM the components tree.

## 2. Data types per structured type

Two typed maps in `src/components/Questionnaire/structured/types.ts`:
- `StructuredDataMap` (`types.ts:27-39`) — what the UI edits (lives in `response.values[0].value` as an array):
  - `allergy_intolerance` → `AllergyIntoleranceRequest` (`src/types/emr/allergyIntolerance/allergyIntolerance.ts:41-51`)
  - `medication_request` → `MedicationRequestCreate` (`src/types/emr/medicationRequest/medicationRequest.ts:435-438`, has `create_prescription` + `dirty` flags)
  - `symptom` → `SymptomRequest` (`src/types/emr/symptom/symptom.ts:55-69`)
  - `diagnosis` → `DiagnosisRequest` (`src/types/emr/diagnosis/diagnosis.ts:69-84`, has `dirty: boolean`)
  - `medication_statement` → `MedicationStatementRequest` (`src/types/emr/medicationStatement.ts:58`)
  - `encounter` → `EncounterEdit`; `appointment` → `CreateAppointmentQuestion` (`src/types/scheduling/schedule.ts:277`); `files` → `FileUploadQuestion` (`src/types/files/file.ts:32-34`, holds a raw `File`); `time_of_death` → `string`; `service_request` → `ServiceRequestApplyActivityDefinitionForm` (`src/types/emr/serviceRequest/serviceRequest.ts:95`); `charge_item` → `ApplyChargeItemDefinitionRequest` (`src/types/billing/chargeItem/chargeItem.ts:77-86`)
- `StructuredRequestMap` (`types.ts:42-56`) — the wire body per type (mostly `{ datapoints: X[] }` upsert envelopes; `encounter` is a bare `EncounterEdit` PUT; `charge_item` wraps in `{ requests }`).
- `ResponseValue` union (`src/types/questionnaire/form.ts:24-41`) enumerates a variant per structured type — **but `service_request` was never added**; `ServiceRequestQuestion` bypasses the union by typing its callback `values: any[]` (`ServiceRequestQuestion.tsx:104-108`) and still emits `{ type: "service_request", ... }` (`:596` etc.). Closed-union rot in action.

## 3. How each legacy component captures data (`src/components/Questionnaire/QuestionTypes/`)

All follow "value lives in `questionnaireResponse.values[0].value`, every edit re-emits the whole array via `updateQuestionnaireResponseCB`". Sizes and UX:

| Type | Component (lines) | Capture UX |
|---|---|---|
| allergy_intolerance | `AllergyQuestion.tsx` (891) | Desktop: inline editable `Table` (`:683-717`); mobile: `Collapsible` cards (`:720-844`) + `EntitySelectionDrawer` bottom sheet for new entries (`:848-880`); add via `ValueSetSelect` typeahead (`:882-888`). **Prefetches existing patient allergies and seeds them into the response via useEffect** (`:575-598`). Delete = soft (`verification_status: "entered_in_error"`) for saved rows, splice for new (`:627-658`). |
| symptom | `SymptomQuestion.tsx` (1013) | Same table/collapsible/drawer trio; prefetch existing at `:670-696`. |
| diagnosis | `DiagnosisQuestion.tsx` (1017) | Same trio; prefetch at `:381-400`; rows carry `dirty` so only edited ones submit. |
| medication_statement | `MedicationStatementQuestion.tsx` (994) | Same trio (`:156-221`); prefetch at `:171-190`. |

content.thinking:
The report reveals a critical architectural issue: legacy structured components are mixing server-sourced data with user input in the same state atom, which creates a dangerous scenario for autosave where restoring a draft could inadvertently resurrect stale server records that should have been removed.

I'm weighing a pragmatic solution: autosave should serialize non-structured responses unconditionally, while structured responses get a per-type draftPolicy that defaults to "exclude" for all legacy adapted types (since their state is conflated with server data), with "serialize" available as an opt-in for future natively-built types. This is honest about the limitation and makes it fixable later, though it does mean a clinician loses unsaved medication rows if the form crashes—a real usability tradeoff worth acknowledging.

For the reference_id collision issue, I'm planning to use a new format like `structured:{type}:{question_id}` to ensure uniqueness per question instance, since the backend just echoes back whatever the client sends. And I need to move StructuredQuestionType into the types layer so components import from there instead of the other way around.

The cleanest approach is to define a canonical `STRUCTURED_QUESTION_TYPES` array in the types layer with a union derived from it, then have StructuredFormData re-export that to avoid touching legacy code. I also need to add the missing `service_request` variant to the ResponseValue union and consolidate the duplicated context requirements into the new registry.

The design is mostly locked in now — what's left is purely visual work from Figma: tab labels, header and footer layout, the autosave indicator, how clinical history rows render, whether multiple questionnaires stack together, and mobile behavior considerations.

Since Figma is still in progress, the most productive next step is updating the spec draft with these structured findings: the draftPolicy rationale, the reference_id scheme, and the type-layer reorganization.

I've identified critical issues in the design: legacy structured components mix prefetched server rows with user input in the same array, which explains why drafts are disabled and why local autosave must exclude these types to avoid stale snapshot hazards. I'm updating the spec to address these findings and the inverted dependency problem with error mapping.

rewritten — rewriting 11 clinical widgets is out of scope. The v2
`renderer/structured/registry.tsx` (component + requires) folds into this
registry; `StructuredSlot` reads from it. Validators move out of
`QuestionnaireForm.tsx`'s map (and the unwired `service_request` validator
gets wired); request builders port from `structured/handlers.ts` (legacy
keeps its own copies until its deletion PR). Adding a new structured type
= one definition file + one registry entry + i18n + backend support.

Type-layer fixes riding along (all additive, legacy untouched):

- `StructuredQuestionType` moves to the types layer
  (`src/types/questionnaire/structured.ts` declares the canonical
  `STRUCTURED_QUESTION_TYPES` array + union); `data/StructuredFormData.tsx`
  imports it and types `STRUCTURED_QUESTIONS` against it instead of being
  the source — fixes the types→components inversion without touching
  legacy consumers.
- The `ResponseValue` union gains its missing `service_request` variant
  (closed-union drift; `ServiceRequestQuestion` currently punches through
  with `values: any[]`).
- Structured batch entries get unique `reference_id`s
  (`structured:{type}:{question_id}`) so error mapping survives two
  questions of the same structured type — legacy assumed at most one
  instance per type.

- Engine: `store.sub(responsesAtom, …)` on the host-owned jotai store;
  debounced (~1.5s) serialize of `{schemaVersion, savedAt, userId,
  questionnaireId, questionnaireVersionMarker, subject, responses, notes}`.

  with `draftPolicy: "exclude"` — their values arrays conflate prefetched
  server rows with user input (the components seed responses from server
  fetches in `useEffect`), so restoring a stale snapshot and re-upserting
  it is a clinical-safety hazard (it can clobber edits made elsewhere) —
  the same reason legacy server drafts exclude structured questions. The
  contract supports `"serialize"` so future natively-built structured
  types (with clean input-only state) get autosave for free. The restore
  bar states when structured answers weren't covered.

content.text:
**Status update — discovery is nearly complete; waiting on the Figma frame digests before finalizing the design.**

What's established so far:

**The task**: rebuild the clinician **fill experience** (the deferred phase noted in the v2 README) as a new stacked branch on top of `bodhi/questionnaire-wysiwyg-builder` (PR [#16619](https://github.com/ohcnetwork/care_fe/pull/16619)).

**Key findings from the deep-dive** (5 parallel code readers + my own reading, all done):

1. **The v2 engine is fill-ready except the host.** `FormMode` already includes `"fill"`, `collectRequiredErrors` is a pure unwired seam, `errorsAtom` has readers but no writer, and every block carries a `data-question-id` scroll anchor. What's missing is exactly one module: the fill host page.

2. **The structured-type scatter is worse than expected** — adding one type today touches ~9 files across two layers, with proven drift (`service_request` has no `ResponseValue` variant and its validator was never wired). The new design is a single `StructuredTypeDefinition` contract (component + requires + validate + buildRequests + draftPolicy) in one total registry — a missing member becomes a compile error.

3. **Autosave has a clinical-safety wrinkle**: legacy structured components seed their response values from **server prefetches** (existing allergies, medications, etc. mixed with user input). That's why server drafts exclude structured questions today. So local autosave will serialize all regular answers, but adapted legacy structured types default to `draftPolicy: "exclude"` — restoring a stale snapshot could re-upsert outdated clinical rows. The contract lets future natively-built types opt into serialization.

4. **Storage conventions are pinned**: `care_qn_fill_draft--{userId}--{subjectKey}--{questionnaireId}` keys, prefix-sweep eviction registered in Login/signOut/appVersion (the repo deliberately keeps patient data out of localStorage, so eviction wiring is mandatory), silent restore with a dismissible "draft restored — Discard" bar, 24h TTL.

5. **The mounting contract is fixed**: four route shapes in `ConsultationRoutes.tsx`, relative `questionnaire/...` links from encounter quick-actions, `?continue_draft=`/`?toDischarge=` params, fixed pseudo-questionnaire slugs, and post-submit navigation to the updates tab — all must keep working.

The draft spec is at [docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-02-questionnaire-fill-design.md](docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-02-questionnaire-fill-design.md). The 9 Figma frame-analysis agents are still running (the desktop MCP is slow, so they run in waves) — when they land I'll finalize the UI sections (exact tab anatomy, header, footer, clinical-history rows, autosave indicator), then write the implementation plan and start building on the new branch.

I'm realizing that the 1200px frame variants actually represent the no-sidebar layout rather than the clinical-history tab view. The evidence points to an off-canvas element suggesting a second tab surface, but there's no frame that actually shows the Patient Clinical History tab in its open state.

Looking at the existing app structure, the clinical-history content should reuse the ClinicalHistoryPage's NavTabs components (responses, symptoms, diagnoses, allergies, medications) inside the second tab. The five filter pills I'm seeing in the floating panel align perfectly with these tab categories, matching what's already built in the app.

I'm also noting the per-question history buttons with clock icons that appear in the structured questions (like "Symptom History" and "Medication History") — these open history popovers and could wire to the clinical history tab, though that's a follow-up rather than core scope.

For the form itself: there's a "Save Changes" button with green gradient styling, a "Cancel" option, and a Draft chip in the tab header, plus a close X on the tab bar (similar to the studio's fullscreen viewport shell). Questions are numbered like "7.1 Core Vitals" and the vitals sub-cards match the SectionCard depth styling. The reference design shows circle radio buttons for options with ≤5 choices, but the current ChoiceInput component uses chips instead — I'm weighing whether to restyle it to match the reference's plain radio circles or keep the existing chip behavior since the specs and studio canvas already assert that pattern.

Restyling the ChoiceChip to circle-radio style would affect the studio canvas too, which is actually fine for design consistency, though there's a small risk of spec text collisions. The change is contained to the component's classes and the role stays as radio, so it's low risk. There's also a medication search combobox with a catalog dropdown that filters by All/Personal/Formulary/Org/Catalog, includes favorites, and shows categories — but that's part of a larger medication_request widget redesign that the Figma shows as a completely new picker design, which is beyond adapting the legacy components we're working with.

Rebuilding the MedicationRequestQuestion is explicitly out of scope since we're adapting, not rewriting. The structured contract we're using enables rebuilding widgets later, one per PR, so I'm keeping the legacy medication widget in its current form as a deliberate divergence from the reference. Trying to rebuild both medication and symptom widgets natively in this PR would be too much scope creep.

The symptom table design is actually quite close to what we already have on desktop — both use a table structure with columns for symptom, dates, status, severity, verification, and notes. So adapting the legacy widgets should look reasonably similar to the reference design.

Now I'm locking down the remaining key decisions for the spec: the fullscreen viewport shell layout with a tab bar showing the questionnaire and patient clinical history, a patient header with demographics and identifiers, and a sub-header strip with badges for blood group and allergies plus the action buttons.

For the responsive layout, I'm thinking a left sidebar with question navigation on larger screens (≥lg), but removing it on smaller viewports. The main content column stays centered at 768px, though structured tables can expand wider — I might need to adjust the canvas container's max-width constraint to let these blocks break out and use the full available space up to around 1048-1108px as shown in the reference.

The tricky part is balancing this without affecting the studio canvas or making all blocks widen. I could either scope a wider container class to the fill layout specifically, or add a QuestionShell wrapper that handles the width policy per question type — letting structured questions break out while keeping non-structured content centered. I'm leaning toward keeping it simple rather than over-engineering a complex per-question width system.

For the outline sidebar, I can reuse the existing QuestionTreeNav component with completion adornments showing answered checkmarks pulled from the responses state. The sub-header needs blood group and allergies badges from patient data, and I notice ClinicalHistoryOverview already has that pattern, so I can reuse those components. The main action button is a "Save Changes" submit with a green gradient, though I'm still thinking through the interaction flow there. Thinking through the Cancel behavior — it should navigate back while keeping the draft persisted locally via autosave, avoiding any destructive discard without explicit user action. For i18n, I'll reuse existing keys like "save_changes" from studio and "cancel" where they're already defined. For the second tab, I need to embed the clinical history tab set by extracting the tab-content mapping from the existing Patient History page into a reusable component.

I'm also adding a "Draft" chip on the Questionnaire tab when unsaved changes exist, plus a restored-draft notification bar. Mobile layout stays consistent with the 1200px design — tabs remain scrollable. On the multi-questionnaire question: the reference shows a single questionnaire per session, so the new fill page will handle one questionnaire at a time via route parameter, matching that pattern.

The no-id route becomes a picker page with search functionality that navigates to the specific questionnaire. I'm dropping the legacy mid-session "add another questionnaire" flow since the launcher dialog and quick actions cover that workflow. I need to finalize the spec by rewriting the UI design section with the actual evidence, updating the out-of-scope items (per-question history buttons, medication combobox redesign, launcher dialog redesign), removing the multi-questionnaire confirmation note, and fixing the "Status: DRAFT" label.

I should also update the test strategy to account for legacy fill specs migrating and label changes. Before writing the final spec, I'll quickly verify that `QuestionTreeNav` is in the shared directory and check its API, plus confirm `ClinicalHistoryOverview` exists as described. Then I'll move into the implementation plan using the writing-plans skill, skipping the user review gate since we're in autonomous mode.

I've confirmed the frame shows the fill view at 1200px without the sidebar, meaning the outline rail is a large-screen affordance and tab 2 sits off-canvas—so I'll reuse the existing clinical-history building blocks for that content. Now I'll verify the two reuse targets and finalize the spec.

## UI design (from Figma evidence — 8 frame digests + metadata pass)

Fullscreen viewport shell (no app sidebar — same `PATHS_WITHOUT_SIDEBAR`
treatment as the studio), top to bottom:

1. **Tab bar**: "Questionnaire" tab carrying a "Draft" chip (indigo badge,
   `bg #e0e7ff / text #312e81`) when unsaved local changes exist;
   "Patient Clinical History" tab; a bordered square close "X" at the far
   right → navigates back to the encounter/patient updates tab.
2. **Patient header**: 48px avatar, name, "42 Y, Male" line; meta pairs
   "Start Date / End Date / Hospital Identifier / Assigned Doctor" (from
   the encounter). Reuses existing patient-header pieces where they fit.
3. **Sub-header strip** (single gray band): left — "Blood Group:" badge +
   "Allergies:" badges (same data sources as
   `clinical-history-overview.tsx`: `BLOOD_GROUP_LONG__*`, confirmed
   allergies); right — "Cancel" (underlined text button) + "Save Changes"
   (primary green gradient `#047857→#065f46`, check icon). Save Changes =
   submit; Cancel = back to updates (local draft survives — no destructive
   discard without the explicit affordance on the restore bar).
4. **Body**:
   - ≥lg (1440 frames): 320px left outline sidebar — `QuestionTreeNav`
     with a `rowAdornment` completion icon per question (answered =
     double-check, unanswered = dot), derived from the live store.
     <lg (1200 frames): no sidebar.
   - Main column: questionnaire title + description header, then the
     one-scroll `form/` canvas in `mode="fill"`. Regular questions render
     in a centered 768px column; structured questions break out to full
     width (~1108px). Implemented via the existing chrome seam: the fill
     host passes a `QuestionShell` that width-constrains non-structured
     leaves and lets structured blocks span — zero engine changes.
   - Question anatomy already matches the shipped `form/` renderer
     (accent bar, number, label, note affordance behind a divider,
     numbered sub-group cards like "7.1 Core Vitals"). The reference
     renders ≤5-option choices as circle radios rather than chips —
     `ChoiceChip` gets restyled to the circle-radio look (roles/names
     unchanged, so specs keep passing).
5. **Tab 2 — Patient Clinical History**: no frame shows it open (its
   surface is parked off-canvas in the design), so the content is an
   adaptation: extract the tab map of `src/pages/Patient/History/index.tsx`
   (responses / symptoms / diagnoses / allergies / medications /
   diagnostic reports) into a reusable `ClinicalHistoryPanel` and embed it
   as pill tabs inside tab 2. The standalone history page keeps working by
   consuming the same panel.
6. **Launch surfaces stay as-is** (overview quick actions, forms dialog,
   command dialog). The redesigned form-launcher dialog and encounter
   overview in the reference frames are separate work.

The design shows no autosave indicator (only the Draft chip + manual Save
Changes); autosave is silent, surfaced only through the Draft chip and the
restore bar.

content.content:
1	# Questionnaire Fill Experience (v2) — Design Spec
2	
3	Date: 2026-08-02
4	Status: Autonomous run (user directive; interactive gates skipped).
5	Reference UI: Figma `Care - Master` node `43604-21509` (section: 8 "Patient
6	Encounter questionnaire" frames + 2 "Encounter_Overview_in-progress" frames).
7	Branch: `bodhi/questionnaire-fill` (new), stacked PR onto
8	`bodhi/questionnaire-wysiwyg-builder` (#16619 → #16618 → develop).
9	
10	## Goal
11	
12	Re-engineer the clinician data-entry ("fill") experience on the v2 engine:
13	
14	- The Figma reference: a two-tab fill page — tab 1 is the questionnaire
15	  data-entry canvas, tab 2 is a clinical-history section — replacing the
16	  legacy `EncounterQuestionnaire` + `QuestionnaireForm` page.
17	- Local autosave: simple interruptions (reload, crash, accidental nav) must
18	  not lose in-progress answers.
19	- Structured questions re-architected behind one extensible contract so new
20	  structured types are added in one place, not five.
21	- Stacked PR, new branch; rearchitect whatever the quality bar needs.
22	
23	User directives, verbatim intent: "the user needs to be re-engineered now";
24	"reference implementation as 2 tabs, 2nd tab is clinical history section";
25	"data entry section should also support autosave in local so that simple
26	interruptions doesn't clear the data"; "The structured should be engineered
27	correctly so that we can also add more structured questions later"; "work a
28	new branch and make it a stack PR"; "feel free to rearchitect everything
29	required to make this a maintainable high quality system".
30	
31	## Current state (evidence)
32	
33	- v2 `form/` renderer is fill-ready except the host: `FormMode` already has
34	  `"fill"`; `validation.ts:collectRequiredErrors` is a pure seam with no
35	  caller; `errorsAtom` has readers and no writer; `StructuredSlot` passes a
36	  stub `clearError`; every block carries a `data-question-id` scroll anchor
37	  (see `QuestionnaireV2/README.md` + form-engine map).
38	- Legacy fill (`src/components/Questionnaire/QuestionnaireForm.tsx`, ~1200
39	  lines) is the behavior reference: one `batchApi.batchRequest` call —
40	  structured answers become raw domain-API requests via
41	  `structured/handlers.ts`, plain answers POST to
42	  `/api/v1/questionnaire/{id}/submit/` (hand-built URL; the typed
43	  `questionnaireApi.submit` route is stale), optional draft-completion PUT.
44	  Known legacy defects to fix, not port: server-error → form mapping by
45	  array position instead of `reference_id`; only 5/11 structured types have
46	  client validators; `clearError` wipes all of a form's errors on any
47	  response change.
48	- Structured extensibility is scattered across 5 places today: type list
49	  (`data/StructuredFormData.tsx`), component (`QuestionTypes/*`), submit
50	  handler (`structured/handlers.ts`), validator map (inside
51	  `QuestionnaireForm.tsx`), context requirements (v2
52	  `structured/registry.tsx`), plus data/request type maps
53	  (`structured/types.ts`).
54	- Drafts today are server-side (`/api/v1/form_submission/`), flag-gated
55	  (`careConfig.enableQuestionnaireDraft`, default false), manual-save only,
56	  and excluded for structured questions/multi-form sessions. There is NO
57	  local autosave anywhere in the repo. localStorage conventions: keys
58	  `care_<feature>--${scopeId}`, `clearXCache()` prefix sweeps registered in
59	  `Login.tsx` handleSubmit and `appVersion.ts:clearAllCaches`; jotai
60	  `atomWithStorage` per-entity via `atomFamily`; PHI deliberately kept out
61	  of localStorage today — a local draft layer must wire eviction into
62	  signOut as well.
63	- Mounting contract (must keep working): the four route shapes in
64	  `ConsultationRoutes.tsx:96-157`; relative `questionnaire/...` hrefs from
65	  encounter QuickActions/FavoriteForms/FormsDialog/EncounterCommandDialog;
66	  `?continue_draft=`, `?toDischarge=true`, FIXED_QUESTIONNAIRES pseudo-form
67	  slugs; post-submit navigation to the encounter/patient `updates` tab.
68	
69	## Architecture
70	
71	New module `src/components/QuestionnaireV2/fill/` (peer of `studio/`),
72	plus a new engine-level `structured/` contract. The legacy
73	`src/components/Questionnaire` fill stack stays in-tree untouched (it is
74	removed in a later PR of the stack, after review), but the fill ROUTES move
75	to the new page in this PR — same replacement strategy the studio phase
76	used for the builder routes.
77	
78	### `fill/` — the fill host (page, tabs, autosave, submit)
79	
80	- `QuestionnaireFillPage.tsx` — route-mounted host: loads the
81	  questionnaire (or FIXED pseudo-form), the encounter, mounts
82	  `QuestionnaireFormProvider` itself (studio pattern — the host owns the
83	  jotai store instance so submit/autosave can read atoms imperatively),
84	  renders header + tabs + footer.
85	- Two tabs per the reference: data entry (the `form/` canvas in
86	  `mode="fill"`) and clinical history (reusing the existing
87	  patient-history components). Exact tab anatomy per Figma evidence
88	  (section below).
89	- `useSubmitQuestionnaire.ts` — the errorsAtom writer: runs
90	  `collectRequiredErrors` + structured validators from the registry, writes
91	  failures into `errorsAtom`, scrolls to first error via
92	  `data-question-id`; on pass composes the batch via `composeBatch` and

# Questionnaire Fill Experience (v2) — Design Spec

Date: 2026-08-02
Status: Autonomous run (user directive; interactive gates skipped).
Reference UI: Figma `Care - Master` node `43604-21509` (section: 8 "Patient
Encounter questionnaire" frames + 2 "Encounter_Overview_in-progress" frames).
Branch: `bodhi/questionnaire-fill` (new), stacked PR onto
`bodhi/questionnaire-wysiwyg-builder` (#16619 → #16618 → develop).

## Goal

Re-engineer the clinician data-entry ("fill") experience on the v2 engine:

- The Figma reference: a two-tab fill page — tab 1 is the questionnaire
  data-entry canvas, tab 2 is a clinical-history section — replacing the
  legacy `EncounterQuestionnaire` + `QuestionnaireForm` page.
- Local autosave: simple interruptions (reload, crash, accidental nav) must
  not lose in-progress answers.
- Structured questions re-architected behind one extensible contract so new
  structured types are added in one place, not five.
- Stacked PR, new branch; rearchitect whatever the quality bar needs.

User directives, verbatim intent: "the user needs to be re-engineered now";
"reference implementation as 2 tabs, 2nd tab is clinical history section";
"data entry section should also support autosave in local so that simple
interruptions doesn't clear the data"; "The structured should be engineered
correctly so that we can also add more structured questions later"; "work a
new branch and make it a stack PR"; "feel free to rearchitect everything
required to make this a maintainable high quality system".

## Current state (evidence)

- v2 `form/` renderer is fill-ready except the host: `FormMode` already has
  `"fill"`; `validation.ts:collectRequiredErrors` is a pure seam with no
  caller; `errorsAtom` has readers and no writer; `StructuredSlot` passes a
  stub `clearError`; every block carries a `data-question-id` scroll anchor
  (see `QuestionnaireV2/README.md` + form-engine map).
- Legacy fill (`src/components/Questionnaire/QuestionnaireForm.tsx`, ~1200
  lines) is the behavior reference: one `batchApi.batchRequest` call —
  structured answers become raw domain-API requests via
  `structured/handlers.ts`, plain answers POST to
  `/api/v1/questionnaire/{id}/submit/` (hand-built URL; the typed
  `questionnaireApi.submit` route is stale), optional draft-completion PUT.
  Known legacy defects to fix, not port: server-error → form mapping by
  array position instead of `reference_id`; only 5/11 structured types have
  client validators; `clearError` wipes all of a form's errors on any
  response change.
- Structured extensibility is scattered across 5 places today: type list
  (`data/StructuredFormData.tsx`), component (`QuestionTypes/*`), submit
  handler (`structured/handlers.ts`), validator map (inside
  `QuestionnaireForm.tsx`), context requirements (v2
  `structured/registry.tsx`), plus data/request type maps
  (`structured/types.ts`).
- Drafts today are server-side (`/api/v1/form_submission/`), flag-gated
  (`careConfig.enableQuestionnaireDraft`, default false), manual-save only,
  and excluded for structured questions/multi-form sessions. There is NO
  local autosave anywhere in the repo. localStorage conventions: keys
  `care_<feature>--${scopeId}`, `clearXCache()` prefix sweeps registered in
  `Login.tsx` handleSubmit and `appVersion.ts:clearAllCaches`; jotai
  `atomWithStorage` per-entity via `atomFamily`; PHI deliberately kept out
  of localStorage today — a local draft layer must wire eviction into
  signOut as well.
- Mounting contract (must keep working): the four route shapes in
  `ConsultationRoutes.tsx:96-157`; relative `questionnaire/...` hrefs from
  encounter QuickActions/FavoriteForms/FormsDialog/EncounterCommandDialog;
  `?continue_draft=`, `?toDischarge=true`, FIXED_QUESTIONNAIRES pseudo-form
  slugs; post-submit navigation to the encounter/patient `updates` tab.

## Architecture

New module `src/components/QuestionnaireV2/fill/` (peer of `studio/`),
plus a new engine-level `structured/` contract. The legacy
`src/components/Questionnaire` fill stack stays in-tree untouched (it is
removed in a later PR of the stack, after review), but the fill ROUTES move
to the new page in this PR — same replacement strategy the studio phase
used for the builder routes.

### `fill/` — the fill host (page, tabs, autosave, submit)

- `QuestionnaireFillPage.tsx` — route-mounted host: loads the
  questionnaire (or FIXED pseudo-form), the encounter, mounts
  `QuestionnaireFormProvider` itself (studio pattern — the host owns the
  jotai store instance so submit/autosave can read atoms imperatively),
  renders header + tabs + footer.
- Two tabs per the reference: data entry (the `form/` canvas in
  `mode="fill"`) and clinical history (reusing the existing
  patient-history components). Exact tab anatomy per Figma evidence
  (section below).
- `useSubmitQuestionnaire.ts` — the errorsAtom writer: runs
  `collectRequiredErrors` + structured validators from the registry, writes
  failures into `errorsAtom`, scrolls to first error via
  `data-question-id`; on pass composes the batch via `composeBatch` and
  submits with `mutate(batchApi.batchRequest, { silent: true })`; maps
  server failures back per `reference_id` (fixing the legacy positional
  bug) into `errorsAtom` + a page-level server-error panel.
- `composeBatch.ts` — pure request assembly (unit of the legacy
  `handleSubmit` serialization rules: date → `dateQueryString`, dateTime →
  ISO, unit/coding entries, enabled-question filtering through
  `isQuestionEnabledInState`, structured requests from the registry).
- `useFillDraft.ts` — the local autosave engine (below).

### `structured/` — one contract per structured type

`StructuredTypeDefinition` colocates everything a structured type needs;
the registry is a single total `Record<StructuredQuestionType, …>` so a
missing member is a compile error:

```ts
interface StructuredTypeDefinition<K extends StructuredQuestionType> {
  type: K;
  component: ComponentType<StructuredInputProps<K>>; // typed; kills the "one permitted any"
  requires: StructuredContextKey[];                  // subject keys needed to render
  validate?: (value, question, t) => QuestionValidationError[];
  buildRequests: (data: DataTypeFor<K>[], context) => Promise<FormBatchRequest[]>;
  draftPolicy: "serialize" | "exclude";              // files can't JSON-serialize
}
```

Existing legacy components are adapted (typed thin wrappers), not
rewritten — rewriting 11 clinical widgets is out of scope. The v2
`renderer/structured/registry.tsx` (component + requires) folds into this
registry; `StructuredSlot` reads from it. Validators move out of
`QuestionnaireForm.tsx`'s map (and the unwired `service_request` validator
gets wired); request builders port from `structured/handlers.ts` (legacy
keeps its own copies until its deletion PR). Adding a new structured type
= one definition file + one registry entry + i18n + backend support.

Type-layer fixes riding along (all additive, legacy untouched):

- `StructuredQuestionType` moves to the types layer
  (`src/types/questionnaire/structured.ts` declares the canonical
  `STRUCTURED_QUESTION_TYPES` array + union); `data/StructuredFormData.tsx`
  imports it and types `STRUCTURED_QUESTIONS` against it instead of being
  the source — fixes the types→components inversion without touching
  legacy consumers.
- The `ResponseValue` union gains its missing `service_request` variant
  (closed-union drift; `ServiceRequestQuestion` currently punches through
  with `values: any[]`).
- Structured batch entries get unique `reference_id`s
  (`structured:{type}:{question_id}`) so error mapping survives two
  questions of the same structured type — legacy assumed at most one
  instance per type.

### Autosave (local drafts)

- Storage: localStorage, key
  `care_qn_fill_draft--${userId}--${subjectKey}--${questionnaireKey}` where
  `subjectKey` = encounterId ?? patientId. Follows the repo's
  `prefix--scope` convention; per-user scoping prevents cross-user leaks on
  shared terminals.
- Engine: `store.sub(responsesAtom, …)` on the host-owned jotai store;
  debounced (~1.5s) serialize of `{schemaVersion, savedAt, userId,
  questionnaireId, questionnaireVersionMarker, subject, responses, notes}`.
- Structured values and drafts: every ADAPTED legacy structured type ships
  with `draftPolicy: "exclude"` — their values arrays conflate prefetched
  server rows with user input (the components seed responses from server
  fetches in `useEffect`), so restoring a stale snapshot and re-upserting
  it is a clinical-safety hazard (it can clobber edits made elsewhere) —
  the same reason legacy server drafts exclude structured questions. The
  contract supports `"serialize"` so future natively-built structured
  types (with clean input-only state) get autosave for free. The restore
  bar states when structured answers weren't covered.
- Restore: on mount, a matching draft (same user, subject, questionnaire
  id + version marker, within TTL 24h) is restored silently into the store
  before first paint, with a dismissible "Unsaved draft from HH:MM
  restored — Discard" bar. Mismatched/expired drafts are dropped.
- Eviction: cleared on successful submit and on explicit discard;
  `clearQuestionnaireFillDrafts()` prefix sweep registered in
  `Login.tsx` handleSubmit, `signOut` (AuthUserProvider), and
  `appVersion.ts:clearAllCaches`; expired entries swept on page mount.
- Server drafts (`form_submission`) are orthogonal and unchanged;
  `?continue_draft=` keeps working (restored server draft supersedes any
  local draft for that key).

### Submission pipeline (behavior contract)

Same one-batch semantics as legacy, composed from the v2 store:

1. Validate: `collectRequiredErrors` + per-type `validate` from the
   registry over enabled questions only → `errorsAtom`; abort + scroll on
   failure.
2. Compose: structured `buildRequests` first, then per-questionnaire
   `POST /api/v1/questionnaire/{id}/submit/` with the legacy value
   serialization, then draft-completion PUT when `?continue_draft=`.
3. Submit one `batchApi.batchRequest` (silent); on error map failed
   results by `reference_id` → per-question `errorsAtom` entries +
   page-level panel; on success clear local draft, toast, navigate to the
   updates tab.

`clearError` becomes real: editing a question's response removes that
question's entries from `errorsAtom` (not the whole form's).

## UI design (from Figma evidence — 8 frame digests + metadata pass)

Fullscreen viewport shell (no app sidebar — same `PATHS_WITHOUT_SIDEBAR`
treatment as the studio), top to bottom:

1. **Tab bar**: "Questionnaire" tab carrying a "Draft" chip (indigo badge,
   `bg #e0e7ff / text #312e81`) when unsaved local changes exist;
   "Patient Clinical History" tab; a bordered square close "X" at the far
   right → navigates back to the encounter/patient updates tab.
2. **Patient header**: 48px avatar, name, "42 Y, Male" line; meta pairs
   "Start Date / End Date / Hospital Identifier / Assigned Doctor" (from
   the encounter). Reuses existing patient-header pieces where they fit.
3. **Sub-header strip** (single gray band): left — "Blood Group:" badge +
   "Allergies:" badges (same data sources as
   `clinical-history-overview.tsx`: `BLOOD_GROUP_LONG__*`, confirmed
   allergies); right — "Cancel" (underlined text button) + "Save Changes"
   (primary green gradient `#047857→#065f46`, check icon). Save Changes =
   submit; Cancel = back to updates (local draft survives — no destructive
   discard without the explicit affordance on the restore bar).
4. **Body**:
   - ≥lg (1440 frames): 320px left outline sidebar — `QuestionTreeNav`

     <lg (1200 frames): no sidebar.
   - Main column: questionnaire title + description header, then the
     one-scroll `form/` canvas in `mode="fill"`. Regular questions render
     in a centered 768px column; structured questions break out to full
     width (~1108px). Implemented via the existing chrome seam: the fill
     host passes a `QuestionShell` that width-constrains non-structured
     leaves and lets structured blocks span — zero engine changes.
   - Question anatomy already matches the shipped `form/` renderer

     numbered sub-group cards like "7.1 Core Vitals"). The reference
     renders ≤5-option choices as circle radios rather than chips —
     `ChoiceChip` gets restyled to the circle-radio look (roles/names
     unchanged, so specs keep passing).
5. **Tab 2 — Patient Clinical History**: no frame shows it open (its
   surface is parked off-canvas in the design), so the content is an
   adaptation: extract the tab map of `src/pages/Patient/History/index.tsx`
   (responses / symptoms / diagnoses / allergies / medications /
   diagnostic reports) into a reusable `ClinicalHistoryPanel` and embed it
   as pill tabs inside tab 2. The standalone history page keeps working by
   consuming the same panel.
6. **Launch surfaces stay as-is** (overview quick actions, forms dialog,
   command dialog). The redesigned form-launcher dialog and encounter

The design shows no autosave indicator (only the Draft chip + manual Save

## Test strategy

- New Playwright specs under `tests/facility/patient/encounter/fill/` for:

- Existing legacy-fill specs (`structuredQuestions/*.spec.ts`,

  no-id picker routes mount the new page in a search-first state that
  navigates to the id route. The launcher dialog + quick actions cover

- Per-question "Symptom History / Diagnosis History / Medication History
  / Templates" header buttons from the reference (clock-icon popovers) —

I'm catching a couple of inconsistencies in my review: I mentioned the issue scattered across roughly 6 places rather than 5, and I need to clarify what `questionnaireVersionMarker` actually represents — it's the `version` string field from QuestionnaireRead, though the spec shows a gap where `modified_date` should be included but isn't currently available in the backend.

For restoring drafts before the first paint, the real constraint is that the provider creates the store internally without exposing it, so I need to add an optional `initialResponses` prop to QuestionnaireFormProvider to let the host seed responses at creation time — this is a small, additive engine change. The host would pass initial responses through this prop rather than trying to access the store directly after mounting.

For submit and autosave handlers, wrapping the entire fill page (tabs, header, canvas) in the provider is cheap and solves the problem cleanly — the Save button and autosave logic can then use `useStore()` from jotai inside the provider tree without needing a separate store-handle seam. # Writing Plans

## Overview

Write comprehensive implementation plans assuming the engineer has zero context for our codebase and questionable taste. Document everything they need to know: which files to touch for each task, code, testing, docs they might need to check, how to test it. Give them the whole plan as bite-sized tasks. DRY. YAGNI. TDD. Frequent commits.

Assume they are a skilled developer, but know almost nothing about our toolset or problem domain. Assume they don't know good test design very well.

**Announce at start:** "I'm using the writing-plans skill to create the implementation plan."

**Context:** If working in an isolated worktree, it should have been created via the `superpowers:using-git-worktrees` skill at execution time.

**Save plans to:** `docs/superpowers/plans/YYYY-MM-DD-<feature-name>.md`
- (User preferences for plan location override this default)

## Scope Check

If the spec covers multiple independent subsystems, it should have been broken into sub-project specs during brainstorming. If it wasn't, suggest breaking this into separate plans — one per subsystem. Each plan should produce working, testable software on its own.

## File Structure

Before defining tasks, map out which files will be created or modified and what each one is responsible for. This is where decomposition decisions get locked in.

- Design units with clear boundaries and well-defined interfaces. Each file should have one clear responsibility.
- You reason best about code you can hold in context at once, and your edits are more reliable when files are focused. Prefer smaller, focused files over large ones that do too much.
- Files that change together should live together. Split by responsibility, not by technical layer.
- In existing codebases, follow established patterns. If the codebase uses large files, don't unilaterally restructure - but if a file you're modifying has grown unwieldy, including a split in the plan is reasonable.

This structure informs the task decomposition. Each task should produce self-contained changes that make sense independently.

## Task Right-Sizing

A task is the smallest unit that carries its own test cycle and is worth a
fresh reviewer's gate. When drawing task boundaries: fold setup,
configuration, scaffolding, and documentation steps into the task whose
deliverable needs them; split only where a reviewer could meaningfully
reject one task while approving its neighbor. Each task ends with an
independently testable deliverable.

## Bite-Sized Task Granularity

**Each step is one action (2-5 minutes):**
- "Write the failing test" - step
- "Run it to make sure it fails" - step
- "Implement the minimal code to make the test pass" - step
- "Run the tests and make sure they pass" - step
- "Commit" - step

## Plan Document Header

**Every plan MUST start with this header:**

```markdown
# [Feature Name] Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** [One sentence describing what this builds]

**Architecture:** [2-3 sentences about approach]

**Tech Stack:** [Key technologies/libraries]

## Global Constraints

[The spec's project-wide requirements — version floors, dependency limits,
naming and copy rules, platform requirements — one line each, with exact
values copied verbatim from the spec. Every task's requirements implicitly
include this section.]

---
```

## Task Structure

````markdown
### Task N: [Component Name]

**Files:**
- Create: `exact/path/to/file.py`
- Modify: `exact/path/to/existing.py:123-145`
- Test: `tests/exact/path/to/test.py`

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: [what this task uses from earlier tasks — exact signatures]
- Produces: [what later tasks rely on — exact function names, parameter
  and return types. A task's implementer sees only their own task; this
  block is how they learn the names and types neighboring tasks use.]

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the failing test**

```python
def test_specific_behavior():
    result = function(input)
    assert result == expected
```

- [ ] **Step 2: Run test to verify it fails**

Run: `pytest tests/path/test.py::test_name -v`
Expected: FAIL with "function not defined"

- [ ] **Step 3: Write minimal implementation**

```python
def function(input):
    return expected
```

- [ ] **Step 4: Run test to verify it passes**

Run: `pytest tests/path/test.py::test_name -v`
Expected: PASS

- [ ] **Step 5: Commit**

```bash
git add tests/path/test.py src/path/file.py
git commit -m "feat: add specific feature"
```
````

## No Placeholders

Every step must contain the actual content an engineer needs. These are **plan failures** — never write them:
- "TBD", "TODO", "implement later", "fill in details"
- "Add appropriate error handling" / "add validation" / "handle edge cases"
- "Write tests for the above" (without actual test code)
- "Similar to Task N" (repeat the code — the engineer may be reading tasks out of order)
- Steps that describe what to do without showing how (code blocks required for code steps)
- References to types, functions, or methods not defined in any task

## Remember
- Exact file paths always
- Complete code in every step — if a step changes code, show the code
- Exact commands with expected output
- DRY, YAGNI, TDD, frequent commits

## Self-Review

After writing the complete plan, look at the spec with fresh eyes and check the plan against it. This is a checklist you run yourself — not a subagent dispatch.

**1. Spec coverage:** Skim each section/requirement in the spec. Can you point to a task that implements it? List any gaps.

**2. Placeholder scan:** Search your plan for red flags — any of the patterns from the "No Placeholders" section above. Fix them.

**3. Type consistency:** Do the types, method signatures, and property names you used in later tasks match what you defined in earlier tasks? A function called `clearLayers()` in Task 3 but `clearFullLayers()` in Task 7 is a bug.

If you find issues, fix them inline. No need to re-review — just fix and move on. If you find a spec requirement with no task, add the task.

## Execution Handoff

After saving the plan, offer execution choice:

**"Plan complete and saved to `docs/superpowers/plans/<filename>.md`. Two execution options:**

**1. Subagent-Driven (recommended)** - I dispatch a fresh subagent per task, review between tasks, fast iteration

**2. Inline Execution** - Execute tasks in this session using executing-plans, batch execution with checkpoints

**Which approach?"**

**If Subagent-Driven chosen:**
- **REQUIRED SUB-SKILL:** Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development
- Fresh subagent per task + two-stage review

**If Inline Execution chosen:**
- **REQUIRED SUB-SKILL:** Use superpowers:executing-plans
- Batch execution with checkpoints for review

toolUseResult.originalFile:
# Questionnaire v2

Management, authoring and rendering for questionnaires, mounted at
`/admin/questionnaires` and `/facility/{id}/settings/questionnaires`. It is
the successor to the legacy questionnaire management UI that used to live in
`src/components/Questionnaire` (removed). That directory still provides the
fill-flow renderer (`QuestionnaireForm`, `QuestionTypes/*`, etc.), which v2
reuses (see Legacy imports below); the renderer here currently ships
`preview` and `readonly` modes only.

## Directory map

- `manage/` — list, create, detail, versions, clone; shared form schema
  (`questionnaireFormSchema.ts`) and the save mutation
  (`useUpdateQuestionnaire.ts`).
- `builder/` — the previous question-editor shell plus the model layer the
  studio still runs on: `builderReducer.ts` is the single source of edit
  state (a `Question[]` tree + selection + dirty flag); every edit flows
  through `dispatch`. Save-time rules live in `saveValidation.ts`. The old
  page shell (`QuestionnaireBuilderPage`) is unmounted — the routes now
  mount `studio/` — and is scheduled for removal after review; the editor
  cards (type picker, options, behaviour, visibility, coding,
  sub-questions) live on as the studio's inspector internals.
- `studio/` — the WYSIWYG builder mounted at `{basePath}/:id/edit`:
  left outline, live canvas (rendered by `form/`), right inspector. May
  import from `builder/` (model + cards), `manage/` (metadata form
  pieces), `shared/` and `form/`.
- `form/` — the full renderer (`QuestionnaireFormRenderer`): the whole
  questionnaire on one scroll, live-synced per-instance store (edits merge
  into responses instead of wiping them), a chrome/decoration seam for the
  studio canvas, and the fill-mode seams (`validation.ts`, mode union).
  Shares the engine pieces of `renderer/` (store atoms, inputs,
  registries, sanitizer); the inputs are co-owned — they are
  host-layout-free (each control carries its own full border) and serve
  only `form/` in practice now.
- `renderer/` — the previous paginated display shell. Its engine files
  (`store.ts`, `inputs/`, `questionTypeRegistry.tsx`,
  `sanitizeStylingClasses.ts`, `structured/registry.tsx`) are shared with
  `form/`; its shell files (`QuestionnaireRenderer`, `QuestionField`,
  `QuestionGroupCard`, `TopLevelCard`, `RendererFooter`,
  `RendererContext`, `NoteAffordance`, `StructuredQuestionSlot`) have no
  mounted consumer left — the revision page now renders through `form/` —
  and only the (equally unmounted) old builder page still imports them.
  Both go in the post-review deletion, at which point the engine files
  relocate out of `renderer/`.
- `shared/` — presentation primitives and the pure tree utilities
  (`questionTree.ts`), plus `buildUpdateBody.ts` and
  `downloadQuestionnaireJson.ts`. `manage/` and `builder/` depend on
  `shared/`, never on each other.
- `queryKeys.ts` — the only place TanStack Query keys are built; keys
  constructed elsewhere silently opt out of invalidation.

## Mounting and scope

Pages never read route params. The router injects a `QuestionnaireScope`
(`src/types/questionnaire/questionnaire.ts`) — a discriminated union on
`authContext` carrying `basePath` and the ids that context requires — from
`src/Routers/routes/adminRoutes.tsx` and
`src/pages/Facility/settings/layout.tsx`. Mutation surfaces gate on
`useCanWriteQuestionnaire(scope)`.

## Renderer

Public surface: import `QuestionnaireRenderer` and `renderer/types` only
(legacy shell), or — for the full renderer — `form/FormCanvas`
(`QuestionnaireFormRenderer` / `QuestionnaireFormCanvas`),
`form/FormContext`, `form/chrome` (the decoration seam the studio canvas
implements) and `form/types`. The store, context and registries are
internal — `form/` is the one sanctioned second consumer of `renderer/`'s
engine files, pending their relocation when the old shell is removed.

`QuestionnaireRendererProvider` creates one jotai store per instance,
seeded at creation (never observed empty) and re-seeded only when the
questionnaire identity changes. React context carries the immutable mount
config (mode/subject/questionnaire identity); the atoms are the reactive
copy selectors read. `responsesAtom` is local-only and `errorsAtom` has no
writer until the fill/submit path lands (see the header of `store.ts`).

Updates are full-body PUTs composed by `shared/buildUpdateBody.ts` from the
cached detail entry — `useUpdateQuestionnaire` writes `setQueryData` before
invalidating so the next save never composes from a stale cache. JSON
export (`downloadQuestionnaireJson`) serializes only definition fields;
audit/user fields (`created_by`, `updated_by`, …) must never appear in an
export file.

## Frozen contracts — do not "fix"

- `evaluateEnableWhen` (`renderer/store.ts`) is a behavior-exact port of the
  legacy `QuestionGroup.isQuestionEnabled`: unanswered dependency → false
  for every operator; comparison runs over ALL of the dependent question's

# Questionnaire v2

Management, authoring, rendering and filling for questionnaires. Authoring

`/facility/{id}/settings/questionnaires`; the fill experience mounts on the
encounter/patient questionnaire routes (`ConsultationRoutes.tsx`). It is
the successor to the legacy questionnaire UI in
`src/components/Questionnaire` — the legacy fill stack
(`QuestionnaireForm`, `EncounterQuestionnaire`, `QuestionInput`) is now
route-orphaned and scheduled for deletion after review; its structured
QuestionTypes components live on, adapted behind `structured/`.

## Directory map

- `manage/` — list, create, detail, versions, clone; shared form schema
  (`questionnaireFormSchema.ts`) and the save mutation
  (`useUpdateQuestionnaire.ts`).
- `builder/` — the previous question-editor shell plus the model layer the
  studio still runs on: `builderReducer.ts` is the single source of edit
  state (a `Question[]` tree + selection + dirty flag); every edit flows
  through `dispatch`. Save-time rules live in `saveValidation.ts`. The old
  page shell (`QuestionnaireBuilderPage`) is unmounted — the routes now
  mount `studio/` — and is scheduled for removal after review; the editor
  cards (type picker, options, behaviour, visibility, coding,
  sub-questions) live on as the studio's inspector internals.
- `studio/` — the WYSIWYG builder mounted at `{basePath}/:id/edit`:
  left outline, live canvas (rendered by `form/`), right inspector. May
  import from `builder/` (model + cards), `manage/` (metadata form
  pieces), `shared/` and `form/`.
- `form/` — the full renderer (`QuestionnaireFormRenderer`): the whole
  questionnaire on one scroll, live-synced per-instance store (edits merge
  into responses instead of wiping them), a chrome/decoration seam for the
  studio canvas, and the fill-mode seams (`validation.ts`, mode union).
  Shares the engine pieces of `renderer/` (store atoms, inputs,
  registries, sanitizer); the inputs are co-owned — they are
  host-layout-free (each control carries its own full border) and serve
  only `form/` in practice now.
- `renderer/` — the previous paginated display shell. Its engine files
  (`store.ts`, `inputs/`, `questionTypeRegistry.tsx`,
  `sanitizeStylingClasses.ts`, `structured/registry.tsx`) are shared with
  `form/`; its shell files (`QuestionnaireRenderer`, `QuestionField`,
  `QuestionGroupCard`, `TopLevelCard`, `RendererFooter`,
  `RendererContext`, `NoteAffordance`, `StructuredQuestionSlot`) have no
  mounted consumer left — the revision page now renders through `form/` —
  and only the (equally unmounted) old builder page still imports them.
  Both go in the post-review deletion, at which point the engine files
  relocate out of `renderer/`.
- `shared/` — presentation primitives and the pure tree utilities
  (`questionTree.ts`), plus `buildUpdateBody.ts` and
  `downloadQuestionnaireJson.ts`. `manage/` and `builder/` depend on
  `shared/`, never on each other.
- `queryKeys.ts` — the only place TanStack Query keys are built; keys
  constructed elsewhere silently opt out of invalidation.

Pages never read route params. The router injects a `QuestionnaireScope`
(`src/types/questionnaire/questionnaire.ts`) — a discriminated union on
`authContext` carrying `basePath` and the ids that context requires — from
`src/Routers/routes/adminRoutes.tsx` and
`src/pages/Facility/settings/layout.tsx`. Mutation surfaces gate on
`useCanWriteQuestionnaire(scope)`.

Public surface: import `QuestionnaireRenderer` and `renderer/types` only
(legacy shell), or — for the full renderer — `form/FormCanvas`

  through `sanitizeStylingClasses` — never render author-supplied classes
  directly.

- `evaluateEnableWhen` (`renderer/store.ts`) is a behavior-exact port of the
  legacy `QuestionGroup.isQuestionEnabled`: unanswered dependency → false
  for every operator; comparison runs over ALL of the dependent question's
  values; `normalizeValue` (booleans → "Yes"/"No", numbers → strings) is
  applied unconditionally before any operator. The only deliberate addition:
  literal-boolean condition _answers_ (legacy-corrupt data that could never
  match) pass through the same normalization in equals/not_equals; string
  answers compare byte-identically to the legacy port.
- Boolean enable_when conditions persist the strings `"Yes"`/`"No"`, never
  JSON booleans (`normalizeBooleanConditionAnswer` in `builderReducer.ts`;
  builder load migrates legacy true/false via
  `migrateLegacyBooleanEnableWhen`).
- enable_when resolution goes through `isQuestionEnabledInState`
  (`renderer/store.ts`) — never re-derive it from `evaluateEnableWhen`;
  the required-field pass in `form/validation.ts` consumes the same
  helper, so exactly one resolution exists.
- `styling_metadata.classes` decorates the question's outer container;
  `styling_metadata.containerClasses` lays out a group's sub-question
  container (the builder's layout presets write it). Both are applied only
  through `sanitizeStylingClasses` — never render author-supplied classes
  directly.

## Legacy imports (allowlist)

v2 may import from `src/components/Questionnaire` only: `ValueSetSelect`,
`SelectOrCreateValueset`, `data/StructuredFormData`, the
`QuestionTypes/*` structured components (exclusively via
`renderer/structured/registry.tsx`, which also owns the one permitted `any`
in the renderer), and `OrgSelector`. A new legacy dependency needs a
registry/allowlist entry here, not an ad-hoc reach-in.

## Adding a question type

1. Add the value to `QUESTION_TYPES` and `SUPPORTED_QUESTION_TYPES`
   (`src/types/questionnaire/question.ts`) — the type union, the builder's
   picker and import validation derive from them.
2. Give the type an icon in `shared/questionTypeIcons.ts`
   (`QUESTION_TYPE_ICONS` is a total record — it will not compile without
   one). The picker's tiles and the tree nav's row icons both render it.
3. Implement a renderer input (`renderer/inputs/`) implementing
   `RendererInputProps`; read the response via a discriminant check on
   `values[valueIndex ?? 0].type` (no casts), write positionally through
   `withEntryAt` when `valueIndex` is set (repeats renders one input per
   entry), and register it in `questionTypeRegistry.tsx`. Structured
   sub-types register in `structured/registry.tsx` instead.
4. Add i18n keys (`question_type__*`, description) to
   `public/locale/en.json`.

## Backend gaps (tracked, not worked around silently)

- `AnswerOption` spec has no `display`/`coding` fields — the v2 builder
  therefore does not offer option display text (the column was dropped
  deliberately). The renderer keeps its `option.display ?? option.value`
  fallback for legacy data that still carries a display value.
- `QuestionnaireReadSpec` lacks `modified_date`/`created_date`; the
  Versions tab shows attribution without chronology until they land.
- Revision listing has no "all" page size; the Versions tab requests
  `limit: 100` and surfaces any overflow.
- The read endpoint can return `version` as a bare number; writers coerce
  through `String()` (type-required via `QuestionnaireRead.version`).
